record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: Can causal set theory provide a fundamental reason for the Everpresent Lambda assumption that the mean value of cosmological-constant fluctuations is zero, instead of leaving zero mean Lambda as an input not derived from the fundamental causal set framework?

evidence.quote: Assumption 3: The mean value of Λ about which the fluctuations occur is zero.
This third assumption is the only input to the Everpresent Λ proposal that does not stem from a fundamental aspect of causal set theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the Everpresent Λ proposal, the cosmological "constant" Λ is treated as a fluctuating quantity sourced by an underlying discrete substratum (a causal set), whose value at a given cosmic epoch is modeled as a random variable obeying, schematically, ⟨Λ²⟩ − ⟨Λ⟩² ∼ 1/√V, where V is the spacetime volume to the past of the epoch. The proposal commonly rests on three assumptions: (i) spacetime volume acts as the conjugate variable to Λ in a path-integral-like dynamics; (ii) there is a statistical correspondence (Poisson sprinkling) between the number N of causal set elements and the spacetime volume V they approximate; and (iii) the mean value of Λ about which the fluctuations occur is zero, i.e. ⟨Λ⟩ = 0.

Within the framework of causal set theory — a locally finite partially ordered set (C, ≼) serving as the fundamental discrete substratum of spacetime, equipped with the kinematical correspondence N ↔ V — derive, or rule out a derivation of, assumption (iii) from the fundamental kinematics and/or dynamics of causal sets. More precisely: produce a mathematically well-defined construction (for example, a causal-set action, sum-over-histories, or stochastic process on the family of finite causal sets) from which the property ⟨Λ⟩ = 0 follows as a theorem, rather than being imposed as an independent input.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on Everpresent Λ (Aspects of Everpresent Λ I & II, 2023; cosmological tests papers) continues to treat ⟨Λ⟩ = 0 as an assumption not derived from fundamental causal set theory, with heuristic motivations (random-sign cancellation in an action sum) but no rigorous derivation. A complete quantum-gravity theory is hoped to one day explain it. The question therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Aspects of Everpresent Λ (I)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the main inputs to Everpresent Λ including the zero mean assumption, motivated heuristically by random-sign cancellation but not derived.
status_evidence.claim: Zero mean is still an assumption motivated heuristically.

status_evidence.title: Dark Energy From Causal Set Theory (Luddy, 2024)
status_evidence.snippet: States that there is no proof for ⟨Λ⟩=0 and that a complete theory of quantum gravity would hopefully give insight.
status_evidence.claim: No derivation of zero-mean from fundamental causal set theory exists.

status_evidence.title: Aspects of Everpresent Λ (II): Cosmological Tests
status_evidence.snippet: Continues to take the zero-mean condition as an input when constructing models.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature still treats zero mean as an input.
